results.title: ITME: Inference Tiered Memory Expansion with ...
results.content: ITME implements differentiated fallback policies for cache misses. While a model weight miss inevitably triggers a pipeline stall, a KV cache miss is resolved through dynamic recomputation on the GPU. This design choice avoids the inefficiency of retrieving isolated missing blocks from the remote tier, which would necessitate either suboptimal chunk-sized transfers or complex retrieval logic. Consequently, recomputing the missing KV segments directly on the GPU is more performance-efficient [...] ITME serves as a high-performance memory backend that integrates seamlessly with established tiering mechanisms. Furthermore, its internal hardware-level prefetching complements various scheduling policies, effectively hiding access latency by overlapping data movement with ongoing computation. This synergy allows ITME to maximize KV cache reuse and system efficiency within any established inference hierarchy. [...] mitigates memory capacity and I/O bottlenecks through software prefetching and read-priority scheduling. Overall, ITME enhances conventional CPU-offloading by providing the necessary memory expansion to accommodate large KV cache footprints beyond host memory limits, achieving up to a 35.7% throughput improvement.

results.title: KV cache tiering: Why GPU memory alone won't scale your LLM app
results.content:
KV caches are organized by layer, attention head, and token. Every transformer layer maintains its own cache, meaning a model with dozens of layers accumulates a surprisingly large amount of cached information as a prompt grows. Because every newly generated token immediately references previously generated tokens, this cache must reside as close to the GPU's tensor cores as possible. The KV cache must therefore live in a GPU’s HBM. HBM provides enormous bandwidth, measured in terabytes per [...] As a result, KV cache tiering requires a fundamentally different approach to infrastructure design. The challenge is not merely finding additional capacity for storing cache data, but also efficiently moving large computational artifacts across storage tiers while maintaining the low-latency performance that makes caching effective in the first place.

Achieving this requires several critical capabilities:

### High-throughput bulk transfers [...] These requirements underscore why KV cache tiering differs fundamentally from traditional caching. Conventional cache systems are designed to manage millions of small objects with relatively predictable access patterns. KV cache systems, by contrast, handle a much smaller number of extremely large tensor objects with highly asymmetric read and write behavior. results.title: LAM: What is the KV Cache Hiding? - by Claus Aasholm
results.content:
The LAM result from a revenue perspective was as expected, a couple of per cent above the Q1-26 guidance. However, profitability is increasing at a faster rate, supporting LAM’s operating-leverage narrative.

The manufacturing expansion from prior years is now operational and generates higher volumes without similar cost growth, tool-maturity impacts, warranty costs, or installation costs. [...] The Chinese memory makers were not part of the same oversupply cycle that crushed Samsung and SK Hynix. They were still in build-out and ramp mode throughout 2022-2023, constructing greenfield capacity from scratch. So their equipment spending continued even as Korean and US memory makers slammed the brakes. [...] The geographic perspective shows that the cyclical collapse affected Korea more than China, whose revenue share shot up to 50%.

This is somehow counterintuitive as China also relies on memory tools from LAM, but the Chinese memory companies were in a different state.
